comment: Per-resort corrections applied by pipeline/normalize_osm.py (ADR-036). See whistler-blackcomb.overrides.json for the format. One polygon, relation/10326057 (Sugar Bowl Resort, a multipolygon of one outer and two inner rings). Every named run and lift checked on 2026-10-31 against the resort's 2025-2026 trail map (sugarbowl.com, SugarBowl_Map_sm_2526.pdf, rendered at 8,000 px and read tile by tile) and its lift and trail status list (sugarbowl.com/conditions, 105 runs under 12 lifts with their ratings): every named OpenStreetMap run that the printed map shows carries the map's rating, so no rating changes. Caboose is on the status list (green) but not on the printed map, and OpenStreetMap rates it blue: the harder rating stays (the rule of 2026-10-22 where only a list rates a run). Chipmunk is novice in OSM and green on the map (both draw green). Names that differ from the resort only by an apostrophe, a hyphen, a space or an abbreviation (Steamers, The 58, Shortcut, Hourglass, Silver Belt Runout, Mount Lincoln Express, Crow's Peak Lift) stay as OSM has them; one capitalisation slip is fixed (Lower MacTavish). The map's four terrain parks (Peregrine Ridge S-M, Golden Eagle L, The Condor XL, The Falconry XS-S) get the park flag; The Falconry is already a snow park in OSM, the other three are plain runs there (the status list rates The Condor blue; the printed map wins). Crow's Nest Glades is drawn inside the map's boundary and listed under Crow's Peak, but OSM's polygon holds only 42% of its outline and the area is tagged backcountry, so it is forced in bounds; Lincoln East Face is rated on the map but drawn beyond the boundary at gate C (Crest), one of the four backcountry access gates, and OSM's polygon holds 43% of it, so it stays out of bounds and resorts.json names it in out_of_bounds_named. OSM gaps (shipped as at Palisades Tahoe): Hannes Schroll (black, Mt. Disney), Mac Runout (blue, status list only), Parking Return and Pine Marten are in OSM but not on the printed map. NEIGHBOURS: Donner Ski Ranch, Boreal Mountain and Soda Springs lie on Donner Summit inside the box (the 2 km margin north of the Village Gondola's top reaches past Interstate 80), and OpenStreetMap has no landuse=winter_sports polygon for any of them (checked 2026-10-31: the Overpass window holds two polygons, Sugar Bowl's and Tahoe Donner's, the latter listed as a neighbour in resorts.json), so they cannot be listed in resorts.json neighbours (the neighbour rule needs a named polygon) and each of their lifts and runs is hidden here one by one, as Magic Mountain's lifts are at Big Bear: Donner Ski Ranch (both sides of Donner Pass Road, 8 lifts and carpets), Boreal (north of Interstate 80, 8 lifts and carpets, 3 named parks), Soda Springs (west, 5 lifts and carpets), and two unnamed rope tows by Soda Springs Road in no polygon. Each hide expects the element's kind and name only, so a rating edit at a neighbour never stops Sugar Bowl's build; a polygon mapped for a neighbour later replaces its hides with a neighbours entry. Royal Gorge's cross-country trails (piste:type=nordic, 292 ways in the window) and the resort's tubing lanes (piste:type=sled) are left out by the pipeline's type rule and need no entry; the Sugar Rush tubing hill's carpet is hidden below. Sugar Bowl's own 12 lifts are all in OSM; nothing of the resort's is lost by these hides.

overrides.reason: Peregrine Ridge is one of the four terrain parks on the resort's 2025-2026 trail map (the S-M park off the Christmas Tree Express) and its status list (Terrain Park); OSM maps it as a plain blue run.
Golden Eagle is one of the four terrain parks on the resort's 2025-2026 trail map (the L park off the Christmas Tree Express) and its status list (Terrain Park); OSM maps it as a plain blue run.
The Condor is drawn as a terrain park (the XL park band off the Christmas Tree Express) on the resort's 2025-2026 trail map, which wins over its status list's blue rating and OSM's plain blue run.
Capitalisation slip ('Lower Mactavish'); the resort's 2025-2026 trail map and status list spell the run MacTavish Lower, and OSM's own Upper MacTavish has the capital T.

Crow's Nest Glades is a double black diamond drawn inside the boundary on the resort's 2025-2026 trail map and listed under Crow's Peak on its status list, but OSM's ski-area polygon holds only 42% of the area's outline and it is tagged backcountry, so the pipeline's rule would draw it out of bounds: forced in bounds.

The Sugar Rush tubing hill's carpet by Sugar Bowl Road, between the resort parking and the Village Gondola's base: not a ski lift (the resort's lift list has 12 lifts and one carpet, Flume), outside the ski-area polygon, and it would draw as a lift with no run; hidden as Winter Park's tubing carpet is.
